content_warnings.title: EBA — EU DORA and operational resilience — new publication detected
content_warnings.text: ​The EBA publishes its 2027 Work Programme. Review for relevance to your EU DORA obligations. Always verify at the authoritative source.
content_warnings.authorityName: EU DORA — Digital Operational Resilience Act (EUR-Lex Official Journal)

security.hint: Security incident detected. In ServiceNow, route to your Security Operations team, not standard IT Ops. Consider raising a Security Incident record (sn_si_incident table) separately from the standard incident. Engage your CISO or security lead immediately. In regulated environments, DORA (Article 17(3): defined escalation procedures; Article 19: reporting of major ICT-related incidents) and FCA SUP 15 may require rapid escalation and notification. DORA Article 19 requires notification to competent authority for major ICT-related incidents.

data.hint: Data/Database incident. If personal data may be affected, your Data Protection Officer must be notified immediately. ICO breach notification is required within 72 hours of becoming aware of a personal data breach (UK GDPR Article 33). In ServiceNow, flag the Privacy Impact field if available. DORA operational incident thresholds may also apply for financial services.

thirdparty.hint: Third-party/Supplier incident. In ServiceNow, populate the caused_by field and raise a Supplier Management record if this represents a service level failure. DORA Article 30 sets out key contractual provisions for ICT third-party service providers, including assistance when an ICT incident occurs (Article 30(2)(f)). Ensure your vendor escalation path is active.

preflight_descriptions.payment_regulatory: This incident description contains payment-related terms. If operating in an FCA/PRA-regulated environment, a notification obligation assessment under FCA SUP 15 is required. Payment Services Regulations 2017 (PSR 2017) may also require notification to the PSR. Consider enabling the regulatory flag and engaging your compliance team immediately.
preflight_descriptions.pii_regulatory: The description may indicate a personal data incident under UK GDPR. The ICO 72-hour notification window starts at the point of awareness (Article 33). DPO and Legal engagement is required now. If operating in financial services, DORA operational incident reporting may also apply.
preflight_descriptions.dora_note: Classification criteria and materiality thresholds for DORA are set out in Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1772, and report content and time limits in Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/301. Verify current thresholds with your compliance team before making any regulatory notifications.

fca_sup15.title: FCA SUP 15 — Notification of operational incidents
fca_sup15.summary: SUP 15.3.1R: firms must notify the FCA as soon as practicable of any operational incident that may require immediate attention. For major operational incidents affecting systems critical to regulated services, notification by close of business on the day is expected.

dora_article_17.title: DORA Article 17 — ICT-related incident management process
dora_article_17.summary: Requires financial entities to define, establish and implement an ICT-related incident management process to detect, manage and notify ICT-related incidents (Art. 17(1)). All ICT-related incidents must be recorded, with procedures that ensure root causes are identified, documented and addressed (17(2)). The process must include early warning indicators, classification procedures, assigned roles and responsibilities, communication and internal escalation plans, and reporting of major incidents to senior management and the management body (17(3)).

dora_article_18.title: DORA Article 18 — Classification of ICT-related incidents
dora_article_18.summary: Establishes the criteria by which ICT-related incidents are classified as major. Classification determines whether Article 19 reporting obligations are triggered. The detailed classification criteria and materiality thresholds are set out in Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1772 (published 25 June 2024). Thresholds shown in this tool are a simplified aid — verify against the Delegated Regulation.

dora_article_19.title: DORA Article 19 — Reporting of major ICT-related incidents
dora_article_19.summary: Financial entities must report major ICT-related incidents to their competent authority (Art. 19(1)) by submitting an initial notification, an intermediate report and a final report (Art. 19(4)). Article 19(4) leaves the time limits to the technical standards: under Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/301, Article 5, the initial notification is due within 4 hours of classifying the incident as major and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of it; the intermediate report within 72 hours of the initial notification; and the final report no later than one month after the intermediate report (or latest updated intermediate report). Reporting applies once an incident is classified as major under Article 18.

uk_gdpr_article_33.title: UK GDPR Article 33 — Personal data breach notification
uk_gdpr_article_33.summary: Personal data breach must be notified to ICO within 72 hours of becoming aware, unless unlikely to result in risk to rights and freedoms of individuals. Controller must document all breaches, including those not notified.

itil_notes.version: ITIL 4 — current edition (AXELOS/PeopleCert). Practice guide updates are published periodically. Check axelos.com for amendment notices and latest edition status. This tool's practice definitions are held in this content layer — not compiled into the application — so guidance can update without requiring app changes as ITIL evolves. For organisations running hybrid ITIL environments, adopt at the pace that suits your organisation.
itil_notes.version_readiness: Framework-version readiness: when AXELOS publish a new ITIL edition, updated definitions and version-aware notes will be added to this content file. The tool will surface them automatically via the content update mechanism. ITIL 4 attribution is retained as the current authoritative standard.
itil_notes.incident_definition: ITIL 4 (current edition): Incident — an unplanned interruption to a service or reduction in the quality of a service.
itil_notes.problem_definition: ITIL 4 (current edition): Problem — a cause, or potential cause, of one or more incidents. Problems require investigation to identify root cause and implement permanent fix.
itil_notes.change_definition: ITIL 4 (current edition): Change — the addition, modification, or removal of anything that could have a direct or indirect effect on services.

platform_notes.servicenow_note: ServiceNow field API names in this tool are validated against Washington DC / Xanadu releases. Core ITSM fields (short_description, description, urgency, impact, assignment_group, cmdb_ci) are stable across all releases. Verify custom field prefixes against your instance configuration.
